availableCommands.name: skill:angular-developer
availableCommands.description: Generates Angular code and provides architectural guidance. Trigger when creating projects, components, or services, or for best practices on reactivity (signals, linkedSignal, resource), forms, dependency injection, routing, SSR, accessibility (ARIA), animations, styling (component styles, Tailwind CSS), testing, or CLI tooling.

availableCommands.name: skill:coding-agent-sessions
availableCommands.description: Finds, reads, and reconstructs coding-agent sessions across Codex, Claude, OpenCode, OMO/Senpi, and other local agent logs. Use when asked to find or search past sessions, transcripts, or subagent runs, or to recover what an earlier session did.

availableCommands.name: skill:debugging
availableCommands.description: Runs a hypothesis-driven debugging loop across any language or binary, escalating to orthogonal oracle angles and locking the fix with a failing test. Use for crashes, silent failures, hangs, wrong responses, memory leaks, async misbehavior, or reverse engineering.

availableCommands.name: skill:frontend
availableCommands.description: Builds, styles, and polishes web UI and UX. Use for any frontend, page, component, styling, layout, animation, or visual-quality task, or when asked to make an interface look or feel a certain way.

availableCommands.name: skill:git-master
availableCommands.description: Handles git work: atomic commits, rebase, squash, blame, bisect, reflog, and history questions. Use whenever a task needs a commit or a git-history investigation; skip for ordinary code edits.

availableCommands.name: skill:integration-review
availableCommands.description: Use when reviewing a feature branch or merged work as a whole: checks for cross-slice consistency, duplication, abstraction gravity, dead code, doc drift, and architectural soundness. This is the whole-diff composition-review stage, catching cross-lane seam defects that no single lane's per-slice review can see. Invoke at the end of multi-slice work, before opening a PR, when inheriting unfamiliar code, or as the before-merge integration check. Triggers: 'review the whole branch', 'integration review', 'is this ready to ship', 'second-opinion read', or as the whole-diff gate before merge.

availableCommands.name: skill:openspec
availableCommands.description: Use to plan, specify or implement a behaviour change in a repository that has openspec/. Picks /opsx-propose, /opsx-apply or plan mode; small changes and repositories without openspec/ stay in plan mode.

availableCommands.name: skill:programming
availableCommands.description: Applies strict, modern language practice (typed errors, exhaustive match, TDD) for Python, Rust, TypeScript, and Go. Use for work on .py, .rs, .ts, or .go files.

availableCommands.name: skill:review-work
availableCommands.description: Post-implementation merge gate: run manual QA on the real surface yourself, then use orchestrator-decided review depth (auditor, optionally oracle) with verbatim briefs, stored trailers, and an omo.merge-gate/v2 record validated by validate-gate-record.mjs. Use before calling work done, before a PR handoff or merge, or when the user asks to review completed work.

availableCommands.name: skill:rules-review
availableCommands.description: Review, prune, merge, and re-scope the rule files the omo rules-injector injects (~/.omo/rules, <repo>/.omo/rules, lessons). Use when rules feel too many or noisy, after a burst of new lessons, when a rule fires in the wrong repo or never fires, or as a periodic (monthly) rules hygiene pass. Triggers - 'review rules', 'rules review', 'too many rules', 'clean up lessons', 'prune rules', 'rules hygiene', 'regeln reviewen', 'regeln aufräumen'.

availableCommands.name: skill:visual-qa
availableCommands.description: Runs rigorous visual QA across web, terminal, and paginated surfaces with screenshot evidence and a verdict. Use for any UI build or change, or when asked whether a page, component, or TUI looks right.

availableCommands.name: skill:workspace-health
availableCommands.description: Read-only audit of machine memory and dev-tool scope: which processes really hold RAM (incl. compressed/swapped pages RSS hides), runaway language servers and build daemons, TypeScript projects that sweep in gitignored bulk data, large ignored dirs IntelliJ still indexes, worktree piles. Use when RAM/swap is exhausted, the machine is sluggish, a language server or IDE balloons, or for a periodic workspace audit.
